purpose: Dated primary-source evidence for proposed AI/data/ML and creative recipes in passport 0.2. Documentation revision only; no source, installed skill, role, training or deployment is certified.

interpretation.vendor_docs: Verify the actual operation, model, API/schema, supported platform, rights, cost and version again when binding a project recipe. A current web page is not proof that a package, account or model is available locally.
interpretation.proposal_status: Seven conditional competence profiles/recipes operate within the existing 35 reusable sources and 12 host roles. No new mandatory skill, role, framework or installed selector is proposed. Any later separately packaged skill/module/role requires demonstrated reusable distinct output, benefit on a real task, full baseline preservation and revised exact-composition approval. Source/runtime implementation is not authorized by this documentation revision.

sources.title: OpenAI Batch API
supported_claims: Asynchronous discounted processing has a completion window and endpoint/model-specific support.
Each input needs a unique custom_id; output order may differ from input order.
Expired batches can retain completed results with consumed-token charges; cancel is not immediate proof that in-flight work did not occur.
sources.limits: The current discount/window must not be generalized to unsupported models, video/audio operations or other vendors. No batch was submitted and no actual cost was measured.
sources.verification_method: Read the official documentation or primary paper through the web tool; no provider operation or runtime test.

sources.title: OpenAI Evaluation best practices
supported_claims: Evaluation should be task-specific, representative, iterative and calibrated with appropriate human feedback.
Example metrics and thresholds are examples rather than universal acceptance requirements.
sources.limits: Evaluation methodology does not require anchoring all projects to one vendor's Evals service; current API availability must be rechecked. Logs and production examples still require data authority and privacy controls.
sources.verification_method: Read the official documentation or primary paper through the web tool; no provider operation or runtime test.

sources.title: OpenAI Structured model outputs
supported_claims: Schema-constrained output can still contain substantive mistakes.
Unsupported input and schema/type divergence require handling; JSON shape alone is not domain correctness.
sources.limits: Not an authorization mechanism and not proof of factuality, correct external effects, media craft or production readiness.
sources.verification_method: Read the official documentation or primary paper through the web tool; no provider operation or runtime test.

sources.title: LangGraph Persistence
supported_claims: Checkpointers preserve graph state scoped to a thread; stores can preserve cross-thread information.
An in-memory checkpointer does not survive process restart and production persistence requires an appropriate durable backend.
sources.limits: A checkpoint is not an external provider receipt, a job worker or an exactly-once guarantee for remote effects.
sources.verification_method: Read the official documentation or primary paper through the web tool; no provider operation or runtime test.

sources.title: LangGraph Fault tolerance
supported_claims: A durable reproducible idempotency key also requires support from the external service.
Missing acknowledgement after provider commit is an unknown outcome that should be reconciled before compensation or continuation.
Non-idempotent effects require explicit retry boundaries and protection.
sources.limits: Does not make LangGraph mandatory. Specific timeout/retry features have version constraints that must be pinned in an actual recipe.
sources.verification_method: Read the official documentation or primary paper through the web tool; no provider operation or runtime test.

sources.title: LangGraph Python reference
supported_claims: LangGraph is intended for stateful orchestration with explicit workflow control; higher-level agent abstractions and low-level graph control are different choices.
sources.limits: Framework choice is an architectural inference based on project needs, not a promise of production quality. Native orchestration may already be sufficient.
sources.verification_method: Read the official documentation or primary paper through the web tool; no provider operation or runtime test.

sources.title: LlamaIndex Ingestion Pipeline
supported_claims: Ingestion pipeline caches node plus transformation combinations using hashes and supports persistence.
Docstore-based document management can detect duplicate documents and updates using document identifiers and hashes.
Embeddings are conditional on the downstream pipeline/vector store use.
sources.limits: Caching and deduplication do not establish source rights, tenant ACL, deletion propagation or the correctness of generated answers. RAG remains conditional.
sources.verification_method: Read the official documentation or primary paper through the web tool; no provider operation or runtime test.

sources.title: Scrapy Jobs: pausing and resuming crawls
supported_claims: JOBDIR can preserve pending requests, duplicate-filter state and spider state for pause/resume.
Job storage must be separated per job and persistence has documented limitations.
sources.limits: Not atomicity or exactly-once for dataset commits or arbitrary external effects. No live crawling or rights verification for a particular platform was performed.
sources.verification_method: Read the official documentation or primary paper through the web tool; no provider operation or runtime test.

sources.title: Scrapy AutoThrottle extension
supported_claims: Throttle adapts delay using measured latency and works with concurrency/delay settings.
Target concurrency is not a hard per-domain quota or permission grant.
sources.limits: Respect source policy, actual rate limits, Retry-After, authentication and license separately. No bypass recommendations are authorized.
sources.verification_method: Read the official documentation or primary paper through the web tool; no provider operation or runtime test.

sources.title: Playwright Python Network
supported_claims: Browser automation supports observing, routing and mocking HTTP/HTTPS network requests and responses.
sources.limits: Browser automation does not confer source rights, guarantee extraction stability or justify using a browser when a supported API or static export is sufficient.
sources.verification_method: Read the official documentation or primary paper through the web tool; no provider operation or runtime test.

sources.title: OpenLineage Object Model
supported_claims: Run, Job and Dataset are distinct lineage entities.
Design-time metadata events and observed runtime run events are distinct.
sources.limits: Useful model for interfaces; no requirement to deploy an OpenLineage backend for every local product and no existing compatible implementation was certified.
sources.verification_method: Read the official documentation or primary paper through the web tool; no provider operation or runtime test.

sources.title: scikit-learn Clustering
supported_claims: Different clustering methods and evaluation measures have different assumptions.
Silhouette can evaluate geometric separation without ground-truth labels but favors some cluster shapes and is not a semantic business-quality oracle.
sources.limits: Embedding/cluster choice, semantic coherence, usefulness and stability require actual project evaluation. No corpus was clustered.
sources.verification_method: Read the official documentation or primary paper through the web tool; no provider operation or runtime test.

sources.title: scikit-learn Common pitfalls and recommended practices
supported_claims: Using information unavailable at prediction time produces optimistic evaluation.
Preprocessing and feature selection must be fitted on training data only; splitting before fitting and appropriate pipelines help prevent leakage.
sources.limits: A generic pipeline does not automatically identify all business-specific temporal, group, selection or attribution leakage.
sources.verification_method: Read the official documentation or primary paper through the web tool; no provider operation or runtime test.

sources.title: scikit-learn TimeSeriesSplit
supported_claims: Chronological splitting avoids training on future observations and testing on past observations.
Comparable fold durations assume equally spaced samples; the splitter has explicit gap/window parameters.
sources.limits: Not a turnkey solution for irregular event logs, group overlap, campaign selection or horizon/label maturity.
sources.verification_method: Read the official documentation or primary paper through the web tool; no provider operation or runtime test.

sources.title: scikit-learn Probability calibration
supported_claims: Probability calibration is distinct from ranking/discrimination.
Brier and log-loss scores combine calibration, discrimination and data uncertainty; Brier alone is not a pure calibration proof.
sources.limits: Classifier calibration is not an automatically valid regression prediction interval, uncertainty estimate for every model or guarantee under distribution shift.
sources.verification_method: Read the official documentation or primary paper through the web tool; no provider operation or runtime test.

sources.title: XGBoost Notes on Parameter Tuning
supported_claims: Model complexity, bias/variance and overfitting are data-dependent tuning concerns.
sources.limits: Does not establish that XGBoost is best for a given project, guarantee CPA accuracy or provide a universal parameter set. No XGBoost installation or training was performed.
sources.verification_method: Read the official documentation or primary paper through the web tool; no provider operation or runtime test.

sources.title: LightGBM Advanced Topics
supported_claims: Missing and zero handling are distinct configurable semantics.
Categorical encoding must remain consistent; unseen prediction categories can be treated as missing.
High-cardinality categories can introduce overfitting concerns.
sources.limits: Serving mappings/preprocessing must match the chosen library version and interface. No claim that categorical handling or model selection is universally automatic.
sources.verification_method: Read the official documentation or primary paper through the web tool; no provider operation or runtime test.

sources.title: MLflow Model Registry
supported_claims: A model registry can track model versions, aliases, metadata and lineage to producing runs.
sources.limits: A registry is optional infrastructure, not proof of a trained, deployed, monitored or rollback-tested model. A versioned file manifest may suffice for a small project.
sources.verification_method: Read the official documentation or primary paper through the web tool; no provider operation or runtime test.

sources.title: DoWhy: An End-to-End Library for Causal Inference
supported_claims: Causal analysis requires explicit assumptions and identification before estimation, with robustness/refutation checks.
Predictive association does not alone identify a causal effect.
sources.limits: A methodological primary paper, not a claim that DoWhy can establish causality without defensible assumptions or data. Two attempted current hosted user-guide URLs were unreadable; this paper and the official repository were readable.
sources.verification_method: Read the official documentation or primary paper through the web tool; no provider operation or runtime test.

sources.title: Hugging Face PEFT LoRA
supported_claims: Low-rank adaptation reduces the number of parameters trained through low-rank updates.
sources.limits: Does not guarantee task quality, supported hardware, source-model license compliance or compatibility of every adapter/export/inference backend.
sources.verification_method: Read the official documentation or primary paper through the web tool; no provider operation or runtime test.

sources.title: Hugging Face PEFT Quantization
supported_claims: Lower-bit representations reduce memory requirements and quantization can be combined with parameter-efficient training approaches.
sources.limits: Do not infer that every quantization backend works on Metal, CUDA or CPU, that quantized and merged variants preserve quality, or that a named model fits the owner's Mac.
sources.verification_method: Read the official documentation or primary paper through the web tool; no provider operation or runtime test.

sources.title: MLX documentation
supported_claims: MLX is an array framework designed for Apple silicon with a unified-memory model and supported CPU/GPU device execution.
sources.limits: No inspection or benchmark of the owner's chip, memory, OS, storage, package support or model architecture was performed.
sources.verification_method: Read the official documentation or primary paper through the web tool; no provider operation or runtime test.

sources.title: MLX-LM official repository
supported_claims: MLX-LM supports text generation and low-rank/full fine-tuning, including supported quantized models, on Apple silicon.
Quantization and upload are separate capabilities; package examples can download remote models.
sources.limits: No package installation, weight download, upload, benchmark, training or inference was performed. No example model is adopted as a universal default.
sources.verification_method: Read the official documentation or primary paper through the web tool; no provider operation or runtime test.

sources.title: MLX-LM LoRA and QLoRA documentation
supported_claims: Training memory depends on quantization, batch size, sequence length and selected layers.
Gradient accumulation/checkpointing and reduced layers have performance/quality tradeoffs; train/valid/test data formats and chat templates matter.
sources.limits: A documented example device's memory/speed is not transferable proof for this Mac, exact model, dataset or acceptable final quality. Adapter/merged/quantized serving variants require independent checks.
sources.verification_method: Read the official documentation or primary paper through the web tool; no provider operation or runtime test.

sources.title: Codex App Server
supported_claims: Supported local Codex app-server integration and authentication are distinct from a commercial production API backend serving a product's users.
sources.verification_method: Official documentation read through the web tool during this research.
sources.limits: An owner login or local bridge does not prove production API entitlement, product-user authorization, external deployment or arbitrary cross-host access.

sources.title: scikit-learn Model persistence
supported_claims: Pickle/joblib-based persistence can execute arbitrary code when loading untrusted model artifacts.
sources.verification_method: Official documentation read through the web tool during this research.
sources.limits: A filename/hash is not trusted provenance; loader/resource isolation and format admission require implementation and actual tests.

sources.title: Transformers Models and model loading
supported_claims: Some model loading paths can require remote custom code; that code needs explicit trust review rather than ambient execution.
sources.verification_method: Official documentation read through the web tool during this research.
sources.limits: Do not infer supported hardware/model availability or a complete sandbox from a loader option.

sources.title: Codex Subagents
supported_claims: Subagent configuration and execution use host-specific supported behavior.
sources.verification_method: Official documentation read through the web tool during this research.
sources.limits: A role file is not a launched actor, permission grant, additional concurrency slot or independent sandbox.

sources.title: Codex as a platform
supported_claims: Codex integrations use supported platform interfaces; developer tooling and the runtime of a delivered product are different concerns.
sources.verification_method: Official documentation read through the web tool during this research.
sources.limits: No working integration, login readiness or production deployment was established by reading this documentation.

sources.title: Cursor Agent
supported_claims: Cursor Agent has its own host tools and execution behavior.
sources.verification_method: Official documentation read through the web tool during this research.
sources.limits: No Cursor runtime, login, account entitlement or parity with Codex was verified.

sources.title: Cursor Rules
supported_claims: Cursor has native project/user instruction configuration that should be preserved during handoff.
sources.verification_method: Official documentation read through the web tool during this research.
sources.limits: The URL can redirect in current documentation; do not blindly translate Codex permissions into Cursor rules.

sources.title: Cursor Cloud Agent
supported_claims: Cloud-agent execution is a distinct supported environment with its own setup and boundaries.
sources.verification_method: Official documentation read through the web tool during this research.

composition.priority: Context continuity, professional design and a genuinely working source-backed panel; lower priority does not remove or defer the full data/ML/LoRA/creative scope.

adoption_gate: Compare current and candidate routes on an authorized real task under the same accepted scope, inputs, references, rights, environment and resource envelope. Reject every demonstrated regression in a preserved property or agreed limit; no averaging or compensating tradeoff. Missing evidence keeps the affected gate open.
